q: For a vacuum, κ = 1 and for other insulating materials κ > 1. (2024)
e: The dielectric constant of a vacuum is defined as 1, while for all other insulating materials, it is strictly greater than 1.

q: When one side of a capacitor holds a positive charge, the other side holds an equal negative charge. (2024)
e: The two conductors of a capacitor always carry equal and opposite charges (+Q and -Q).

q: Variable capacitor is used as tuning capacitor. (2024)
e: Variable capacitors are commonly used in radio receiver circuits as tuning capacitors to adjust resonant frequencies.

q: A capacitor is an electrical device that stores electrical energy in the form of a magnetic field. (2024)
e: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field, whereas an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.

q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of a magnetic field. (2024)
e: Capacitors store electrical energy within an electric field between their plates, not a magnetic field.

q: Variable capacitors mostly use air as the dielectric medium. (2024)
e: Air is the standard and most commonly used dielectric medium in variable capacitors.

q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of magnetic field. (2025)
e: Electrical energy in a capacitor is stored electrostatic ally in an electric field.

q: Film capacitors and ceramic capacitors have positive and negative terminals. (2025)
e: Film and ceramic capacitors are non-polarized and do not possess fixed positive or negative terminals.

q: If one conductor of a capacitor has a charge + Q the other has a - Q. (2025)
e: By definition, the charges on the two conductors of a capacitor are equal in magnitude and opposite in polarity (+Q and -Q).

q: The total capacitance of capacitors in parallel is equal to the sum of their individual capacitances. (2025)
e: For parallel combination, total capacitance is given by the formula C_total = C_1 + C_2 + ... + C_n.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor depends on the nature of the insulator between the two conductors of that capacitor. (2025)
e: Capacitance depends directly on the dielectric constant of the insulating material placed between the conductors.

q: Capacitors in parallel have the same charge on each capacitor. (2025)
e: Capacitors in parallel share the same potential difference (voltage), but hold different charges if their capacitances differ.

q: A supercapacitor (SC) is also called an ultracapacitor. (2025)
e: Supercapacitors are high-capacity electrochemical capacitors frequently referred to as ultracapacitors.

q: The dielectric strength of insulating materials is smaller than that of air. (2025)
e: Most solid insulating materials have a higher dielectric strength than air, allowing them to withstand higher electric fields without breakdown.

q: Variable capacitors mostly use air as the dielectric medium. (2025)
e: Air is typically used as the dielectric medium in variable capacitors.

q: Capacitors can also be used in a time-dependent circuit (timer circuit). (2025)
e: Because of their charging and discharging behavior over time, capacitors are key components in timer circuits.

q: When capacitors having different capacitances are connected in parallel, they have the same charge. (2025)
e: In parallel connections, the voltage across each capacitor is identical, but charges vary directly with individual capacitances (Q = CV).

q: A capacitor stores electrical energy in the form of an electric field. (2025)
e: Energy is stored electrostatically in the electric field established between the capacitor plates.

q: The potential difference of the capacitor is twice the potential difference between two conductors of the capacitor. (2025)
e: The potential difference of a capacitor is simply equal to the potential difference existing between its two conductors.

q: A capacitor consists of two conductors separated by a small distance. (2026)
e: A basic capacitor consists of two conductive surfaces separated by a small insulating distance or dielectric gap.

q: The dielectric constant of water is larger than that of vacuum. (2026)
e: The dielectric constant of water is approximately 80, which is significantly larger than that of a vacuum (1).

q: Charging a capacitor means connecting the capacitor to a resistor. (2026)
e: Charging a capacitor requires connecting it across a voltage source (such as a battery) to supply charge, not simply connecting a resistor.
